steps.title: Obtain ethical approval
steps.instruction: Secure Institutional Review Board approval and obtain informed consent before any human tissue or imaging work.

steps.title: Set up IV line and MRI
steps.instruction: Place an 18‑22 G catheter with pressure‑infusion tubing and connect to an MRI‑compatible automatic pressure injector; position the subject in the scanner with a 32‑channel head coil.

steps.title: Acquire baseline MRI scans
steps.instruction: Run the following sequences before contrast injection:

substeps.instruction: Whole‑brain T1‑MPRAGE (sagittal 3D turbo‑fast low angle shot): matrix 256 × 256, isotropic 1 mm, 176 slices, TR/TE/TI = 3000/3/900 ms, flip = 9°, acquisition 5 min 38 s.

Limited T2‑FLAIR (coronal 2D over superior sagittal sinus): FOV 256 mm², 22 slices, in‑plane 0.25 mm², 42 × 3 mm slices, TR/TE/TI = 6500/93/2100 ms, ETL = 17, bandwidth 80 Hz/pixel, acquisition 5 min.
Black‑blood SPACE (coronal): FOV 174 mm², matrix 320 × 320, in‑plane 0.27 mm², 64 × 0.5 mm sections, TR/TE = 938/22 ms, ETL = 35, bandwidth 434 Hz/pixel, acquisition 7 min 50 s.

Whole‑brain T2‑FLAIR (coronal 3D SPACE): FOV 235 mm², matrix 512 × 512, in‑plane 0.46 mm², 176 × 1 mm sections, TR/TE/TI = 4800/354/1800 ms, non‑selective inversion, ETL = 298, bandwidth 780 Hz/pixel, acceleration = 2, acquisition 14 min.
Whole‑brain T1‑SPACE (axial 3D): matrix 256 × 256, isotropic 0.9 mm, 112 sections, TR/TE = 600/20 ms, flip = 120°, ETL = 28, acquisition 10 min.
Acquire 2–3 overlapping coronal slabs to cover most of the cerebral hemispheres.

steps.title: Inject contrast and repeat MRI
steps.instruction: Inject gadobutrol (0.1 mmol/kg body weight) or gadofosveset (0.03 mmol/kg) at 0.3 ml/min, followed by a 10 ml saline flush; then repeat the A3a, A3c, and A3d sequences (the three scans listed above).

steps.title: Process MRI images
steps.instruction: Convert scanner DICOM files to NIFTI using the dcm2nii script; co‑register pre‑ and post‑contrast volumes, perform skull‑stripping, and subtract pre‑ from post‑contrast images in MIPAV (Algorithms → Registration → Optimized Automatic Registration, then Image Calculator → Subtract). Import subtraction images into OsiriX and generate maximum‑intensity‑projection 3‑D renderings (2D/3D → 3D Surface Rendering).

steps.title: Optional gadofosveset imaging
steps.instruction: For dedicated lymphatic imaging, repeat steps 2‑5 using gadofosveset (0.03 mmol/kg) instead of gadobutrol and compare subtraction images to identify dural lymphatic vessels.

steps.title: Fix dura tissue
steps.instruction: Immerse freshly dissected human dura in 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin (NBF) containing <2 % methanol for 24–48 h at room temperature with gentle swirling; then store in 1× PBS with a few drops of 10 % formalin at room temperature.

steps.title: Embed and section dura
steps.instruction: Trim the fixed dura into coronal pieces, embed in paraffin, and cut 3–8 µm sections on a rotary microtome; float sections in 20 % ethanol at room temperature, then transfer to a 44 °C water bath, and mount onto Superfrost Plus Microslides.

substeps.instruction: Keep the paraffin block on melting ice or a cold wet paper towel before sectioning.
After mounting, remove excess water with a quick wrist‑snap, then dry slides vertically overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and rehydrate
steps.instruction: Treat slides with 3 changes of xylene (3 min each), then 3 changes of 100 % ethanol (3 min each), 80 % ethanol (3 min), 50 % ethanol (3 min), and finally rinse in deionized water for 1 min.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval by steaming
steps.instruction: Place a plastic Coplin jar filled with Target Retrieval Solution (pH 9) into a laboratory steamer set to the “Max” water line; steam slides for 20 min at 95–100 °C, then allow the jar to cool 10 min at room temperature, and rinse slides gently in Tris‑buffered saline (TBS) for 5 min.

steps.title: Block endogenous peroxidase
steps.instruction: Incubate slides in 0.3 % H₂O₂ solution (in deionized water) at room temperature for 10 min, then rinse gently in TBST (TBS‑0.5 % Tween 20) for 1 min.

steps.title: Draw PAP barrier
steps.instruction: Use a Super HT PAP pen to draw a hydrophobic barrier around each tissue section, then rinse slides in TBST for 1 min.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Apply 3–4 drops of Dako Protein Block to each tissue, incubate in a humidified chamber at room temperature for 20 min, then gently tap off excess without rinsing.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Dilute each primary antibody in Dako Antibody Diluent (see Table 1 for dilution factors: LYVE1 1:200, Podoplanin 1:50, CD31 1:50, PROX1 1:300, COUP‑TF II 1:200, CCL21 1:200) and apply 100–200 µl to fully cover the tissue; incubate 2 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C in a humidified chamber.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Rinse slides in TBST three times, 5 min each, on a rocker.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Apply HRP‑conjugated anti‑mouse IgG or anti‑rabbit IgG (as appropriate) diluted in antibody diluent, incubate 30 min at room temperature in a humidified chamber.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Rinse slides in TBST three times, 5 min each, on a rocker.

steps.title: Develop DAB chromogen
steps.instruction: Place 3–4 drops of freshly prepared DAB substrate on each slide, monitor development of a brown signal under a microscope, and stop the reaction by dipping the slide in deionized water.

steps.title: Hematoxylin counterstain
steps.instruction: Dip slides in Leica Hematoxylin 560 MX for 10 s, rinse in tap water for 5 min, then immerse in a bluing solution (Leica Blue buffer or 0.2 % ammonia or 0.1 % lithium carbonate).

steps.title: Dehydrate and mount
steps.instruction: Air‑dry slides, apply Permount permanent mounting medium, place a coverslip, and store the mounted slides at room temperature.

steps.title: Simultaneous D2‑40/CD31 IHC
steps.instruction: Follow steps 9‑21, but:

substeps.instruction: Apply a cocktail of D2‑40 and CD31 primary antibodies (in Dako Antibody Diluent) and incubate 2 h at room temperature.
Incubate with HRP‑anti‑mouse IgG (for D2‑40) and ImmPRESS‑AP anti‑rabbit IgG (for CD31) together for 30 min at room temperature.
Develop DAB (brown) for D2‑40, then develop Vector Blue (blue) for CD31; stop each reaction with deionized water.
Do NOT perform hematoxylin counterstaining after the Vector Blue step.
Dehydrate and coverslip with Permount as in step 21.

steps.title: Sequential PROX1/CD31 IHC
steps.instruction: Complete the PROX1 single‑stain protocol through step 21, then:

substeps.instruction: Apply 3–4 drops of Dako Protein Block, incubate 20 min at room temperature, and remove excess (no rinse).
Apply CD31 primary antibody (diluted as above) and incubate 2 h at room temperature.
Wash TBST 3 × 5 min, then incubate with ImmPRESS‑AP anti‑rabbit IgG for 30 min at room temperature.
Develop with Vector Blue substrate (3–4 drops), stop with deionized water, and omit hematoxylin counterstain.
Dehydrate and mount with Permount.

steps.title: Fluorescent D2‑40/CD31 staining
steps.instruction: Follow steps 9‑21 up to primary antibody incubation, then:

substeps.instruction: Apply a cocktail of secondary antibodies: Goat anti‑mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 and Goat anti‑rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 594, each diluted 1:200 in Dako Antibody Diluent; incubate 30 min at room temperature in a humidified chamber.
Wash slides TBST 3 × 5 min on a rocker.
Air‑dry, then coverslip with Fluoro‑Gel II mounting medium.
Observe D2‑40 (green) and CD31 (red) signals by fluorescence microscopy.

steps.title: Prepare TBST solution
steps.instruction: Mix 200 ml of 10× TBS with 1,800 ml deionized water, add 1 ml Tween 20, and stir thoroughly with a magnetic stirrer to obtain 0.5 % Tween 20 in TBS (TBST).
